per_question.question: How does the EPSDT special provision affect coverage for outpatient therapy services, and what ordering practitioner requirements apply to beneficiaries under 21?

Because the EPSDT section text in the graph is truncated, I’m supplementing it with the directly related under-21 and coverage sections so I can answer conservatively and only from retrieved text.## Short answer

For **beneficiaries under 21**, the **EPSDT special provision** can allow NC Medicaid to cover outpatient therapy services **beyond ordinary policy limitations** when the service is medically necessary under EPSDT standards. But EPSDT does **not** waive other procedural requirements: if the therapy service **requires prior approval, prior approval is still required**.

The **ordering practitioner** for outpatient therapy under Policy 10A must be one of the practitioner types specifically listed in the policy: **MD, DO, DPM, CNM, PA, or NP**.

## What Policy 10A says

### 1) EPSDT can create an exception to policy limitations for beneficiaries under 21
Policy 10A includes a dedicated section titled **“EPSDT Special Provision: Exception to Policy Limitations for a Medicaid Beneficiary under 21 Years of Age.”** The retrieved text from that section is truncated in the database, but it expressly cites **42 U.S.C. § 1396d(r)** and includes the usual EPSDT guardrails that services are not covered if they are **unsafe, ineffective, experimental/investigational, or not medical in nature / not generally recognized as accepted medical practice**.  
Cite: **Clinical Coverage Policy 10A, Section 2.2.1 — “EPSDT Special Provision: Exception to Policy Limitations for a Medicaid Beneficiary under 21 Years of Age”** ([Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)), effective **2025-02-01**.

In plain language, that means EPSDT can expand coverage for a child or youth under 21 when outpatient therapy is medically necessary, even if an ordinary policy limit would otherwise restrict coverage.

### 2) EPSDT does not eliminate prior approval requirements
Policy 10A is explicit on this point:

> “If the service, product, or procedure requires prior approval, the fact that the beneficiary is under 21 years of age does NOT eliminate the requirement for prior approval.”

Cite: **Clinical Coverage Policy 10A, unnumbered subsection — “b. EPSDT and Prior Approval Requirements”** ([Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)), effective **2025-02-01**.

So the practical effect is:

- **EPSDT may allow broader substantive coverage**
- but **authorization rules still apply**
- and the provider still has to submit:
  - **the prior approval request**, and
  - **all health records and other records supporting that the beneficiary met the specific criteria in Subsection 3.2**

Cite: **Clinical Coverage Policy 10A, Section 5.1.1 — “General”** ([Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)), effective **2025-02-01**.

### 3) Under-21 coverage is tied to medical necessity
Policy 10A’s general coverage standard says the service must be:

- **individualized, specific, and consistent with symptoms or confirmed diagnosis**;
- **not in excess of the beneficiary’s needs**;
- able to be **safely furnished**, with **no equally effective and more conservative or less costly statewide alternative**; and
- furnished in a way **not primarily for the convenience** of the beneficiary, caretaker, or provider.

Cite: **Clinical Coverage Policy 10A, Section 3.1 — “General Criteria Covered”** ([Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)), effective **2025-02-01**.

Policy 10A also has a separate section on **“Medical Necessity Visit Guidelines for Beneficiaries Under 21 Years of Age,”** which confirms that under-21 therapy coverage is organized around **medical necessity** rather than just the adult visit-limit structure.  
Cite: **Clinical Coverage Policy 10A, Section 5.4 — “Medical Necessity Visit Guidelines for Beneficiaries Under 21 Years of Age”** ([Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)), effective **2025-02-01**.

## Ordering practitioner requirements for beneficiaries under 21

Policy 10A, Section 3.1.2 lists the permitted ordering practitioners:

- **Medical Doctor (MD)**
- **Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO)**
- **Doctor of Podiatric Medicine (DPM)**
- **Certified Nurse Midwife (CNM)**
- **Physician Assistant (PA)**
- **Nurse Practitioner (NP)**

Cite: **Clinical Coverage Policy 10A, Section 3.1.2 — “Ordering Practitioners”** ([Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment)), effective **2025-02-01**.

## Bottom line

For a Medicaid beneficiary **under 21**, **EPSDT can support coverage of medically necessary outpatient therapy services even when ordinary policy limitations would otherwise restrict coverage**. But **EPSDT does not remove prior authorization requirements**, and the service still has to satisfy Policy 10A’s medical-necessity standards and documentation requirements. The therapy must be **ordered by one of the practitioner types listed in Section 3.1.2: MD, DO, DPM, CNM, PA, or NP**.
